summary: Lewin Bentham Bowring (1824–1910) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Chief Commissioner for the Government of Mysore around 1862–1870 and was late Chief Commissioner at the University of Mysore.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his MA at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He has held research posts at the British Museum, Freie Universität Berlin, and the University of Munich, and at Bonn.

Lewis Hodous (1872–1949) studied at Case Western Reserve University, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, he founded and led Fukien Union Theological Seminary before serving as a professor at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster (b. 1932) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned degrees from Roanoke College, Claremont School of Theology, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson, later serving as professor and emeritus at UC Berkeley.

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs (b. 1942) is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He has served as a Professor at Tibet University and as Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Li-ching Chang (1936–2010) worked in Sinology and linguistics, teaching Mandarin Chinese at the University of Washington, Tunghai University, Bryn Mawr College, Harvard University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Swarthmore College.
Liang Cai, a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology, studied under Daniel Boucher. She held a position as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).

Libbie Mills is an Indologist who earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2011. She served as a teacher of Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto (attested 2020).
Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo. She held research posts at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from around 1947 to 1978.

Lilla Russell-Smith works in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and earned a PhD from SOAS University of London.
Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Julius Berugoda and M. Sri Rammandala, and held posts at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970 and 2008).

Limei Chi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Jinhua Chen. She held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and as Professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

Lin He (1902–1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from around 1919 to 1926. He subsequently held an academic post at National Tsing Hua University from circa 1931 to 1952.
Lin Heng is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).
Lin Li is a researcher in computational linguistics who has held posts at Utrecht University and Qinghai Normal University.

Linda Hogan (b. 1964) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Maynooth University and Trinity College Dublin. She lectured at Chester and Leeds, and later served as Chair of Ecumenics and Vice-Provost at Trinity College Dublin.
Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
